body.x: Hudit (CEO Han Deok-hyun, Kim Young-bin) participated in CES 2024 held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 9 (Tuesday) to January 12 (Friday, local time).

Hudit focuses on developing and integrating human-centered artificial intelligence technology into digital therapy. The company aims to provide solutions for individuals with medical blind spots, such as older adults, those with limited mobility, isolated individuals, and patients with congenital disabilities. Utilizing the latest artificial intelligence technology, including motion recognition, facial expression recognition, emotion recognition, and conversation recognition, Hudit strives to develop personalized digital therapeutic solutions, intending to offer therapeutic solutions benefiting everyone through technological innovation.

During CES 2024, Hudi showcased various digital therapy apps and proprietary technologies. These apps and technologies aim to enhance communication abilities for individuals with communication challenges through music, treat anxiety disorders and ADHD, and provide customized management for cancer patients. Each app is developed using HAI (Human-centered Artificial Intelligence) technology and offers personalized therapeutic methods based on scientific evidence and theoretical foundations. Hudit expects to address various health conditions and assist users in managing their health through these solutions.

A representative from Hudit explained, “Participating in CES 2024 focuses on introducing our Human-centered Artificial Intelligence (HAI) technology and related applications. This exhibition will serve as an opportunity to demonstrate how our technology can be effectively applied in everyday life and the medical field.” The goal of Hudit is to explore personalized therapeutic methods through HAI, enhancing the patient experience. At CES 2024, the company aims to network with industry experts, seek collaboration opportunities, and share its vision and technological approach.

The representative stated, “Hudit targets a diverse audience interested in various diseases and digital therapeutic solutions in the U.S. market. This includes healthcare service providers, innovative companies in the digital therapy sector, and investors considering investment in related technologies. Technology collaboration companies exploring new market opportunities through partnerships are also key targets. Hudit seeks to expand growth opportunities in the digital therapy field through collaboration with these diverse groups.”

body.x: Hudit is currently focusing on research involving chatbots based on the Large Language Model (LLM) for counseling and diagnosis in isolated environments and developing deep learning models for detecting post-surgery complications. The representative emphasized that these studies are advancing through the progress of HAI technology. The company plans to create new apps based on this technology and, in the future, utilize advanced technology to monitor and improve user health conditions, aspiring to establish a leading position in the digital therapy field and continually pursue technological innovation.

CES, the world’s largest IT exhibition organized by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), is held in Las Vegas every January, providing a comprehensive view of global technology industry trends. AVING News, covering CES for 18 consecutive years, has been selecting the best innovative products, companies, and technologies and conducting ‘BEST OF CES’ and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA’ selections. Additionally, through ‘AVING LIVE,’ they provide live coverage of CES issues.

The CES 2024 Seoul Pavilion operated on the most historical scale since Seoul’s first participation in CES in 2020, with the largest exhibition area, number of participating companies, and supporter numbers. Seoul Metropolitan Government collaborated with 13 institutions to design The Seoul Pavilion, which is essential in Seoul’s endeavors to establish Seoul as a startup hub. Among the participating companies in the Seoul Pavilion, 17 received innovation awards, proving their capabilities. Collaborated institutions include Seoul Business Agency, Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul Campus Town, Yangjae Innovation Hub, Gwanak-gu, Yonsei University, Korea University, Chung-Ang University, Sogang University, Kookmin University, Hanyang University, and Kyunghee University, totaling 13. Seoul City and institutions and supporters participating in industry-academic cooperation are matched 1:1 with companies, with a maximum of 85 supporters participating.
